title: Define Destructive Color in Tailwind Config
description: Add a semantic 'destructive' (red) color to the Tailwind CSS theme in tailwind.config.ts, following the shadcn/ui convention using CSS variables.
details: Edit tailwind.config.ts to add a 'destructive' color entry (e.g., destructive: 'hsl(var(--destructive))') and a corresponding foreground color. If not already present, ensure these CSS variables are defined in app/globals.css for both light and dark themes. This enables consistent use of the destructive color throughout the UI.
test_strategy: Run `npx tailwindcss -o output.css` to ensure the new color classes are generated. Inspect the output CSS for the presence of 'bg-destructive' and 'text-destructive-foreground'. Visually verify in the browser that the color renders as expected.

title: Add 'Destructive' Variant to Button Component
description: Extend the shadcn/ui Button component to support a new 'destructive' variant using the newly defined Tailwind color classes.
details: In components/ui/button.tsx, update the cva (Class Variance Authority) configuration to add a 'destructive' variant. Use Tailwind classes like 'bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground hover:bg-destructive/90' and ensure all states (hover, focus, disabled) are styled. Do not break existing variants.
test_strategy: Render the Button component with variant='destructive' in isolation (e.g., via Storybook or a test page). Confirm visual appearance and that all states (default, hover, focus, disabled) are styled correctly. Check accessibility contrast ratios.

title: Apply Destructive Variant to Target Button
description: Update the relevant button instance (e.g., 'Create New Key') in the dashboard page to use the new 'destructive' variant.
details: Locate the target button in app/dashboard/page.tsx (or the appropriate file). Change its instantiation to <Button variant="destructive">Create New Key</Button>. Ensure the button's purpose matches the destructive styling (confirm with stakeholders if necessary).
test_strategy: Load the dashboard page and verify the button appears with the new red style. Confirm that only the intended button is affected and that other buttons retain their original styles.

title: Verify Visual Consistency and Accessibility
description: Manually test the new destructive button variant for visual consistency, accessibility, and correct integration with dark mode.
details: Check the dashboard and any other pages where the destructive button might appear. Ensure the color is consistent in both light and dark themes, and that the button meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements. Test keyboard navigation and focus states. Optionally, update or add a Storybook story for the destructive variant.
test_strategy: Use browser dev tools and accessibility checkers (e.g., axe) to verify color contrast and keyboard accessibility. Switch between light and dark modes to confirm consistency. Optionally, run a visual regression test if available.
